issues.body:
The new paragraph ends with the normative instruction: "Always construct query requests with `Request::new(ODRL_READ)`." There is no `ODRL_READ` in the public API. A repo-wide search finds the identifier in exactly three places: this SKILL line, a private `const ODRL_READ` in `gui/src-tauri/src/odrl.rs:242`, and a private `const ODRL_READ` in `crates/sparq-lws-core/src/authz/odrl.rs:44`. Neither is reachable from a downstream crate. `sparq-solid` re-exports only `ODRL_NS` (crates/sparq-solid/src/odrl_bridge.rs:152), and `sparq-policy` exports `ODRL_NS`/`ODRL_PURPOSE`/`ODRL_COUNT`/`ODRL_RECIPIENT`/`ODRL_SPATIAL`/`ODRL_DATETIME` — no per-action constants.

This also contradicts the SKILL's own runnable example roughly three paragraphs above, which correctly writes `Request::new("http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/read")`, and the new test in this same PR, which builds the action via the local `odrl("read")` helper. A reader following the sentence gets an unresolved-identifier compile error. Because this PR's whole deliverable is the documented contract, the normative sentence naming a nonexistent API is the primary artifact being wrong, not a cosmetic slip. The `rust,ignore` fence on the SKILL example means no doctest catches it.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) change the sentence to match the surrounding style, e.g. "Always construct query requests with the concrete read action: `Request::new(\"http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/read\")` (or `format!(\"{ODRL_NS}read\")` using the exported `sparq_solid::ODRL_NS`)."; or (b) if a named constant is genuinely wanted, add `pub const ODRL_READ: &str = "http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/read";` next to `ODRL_NS` in crates/sparq-solid/src/odrl_bridge.rs, re-export it from the crate root, use it in the new test instead of `odrl("read")` so the doc claim is compile-checked, and dedupe the private copies in gui/src-tauri/src/odrl.rs and crates/sparq-lws-core/src/authz/odrl.rs. Option (a) is the smaller, lower-risk change and keeps the core lean.
issues.title: SKILL instructs `Request::new(ODRL_READ)` but no `ODRL_READ` constant is exported by sparq-solid/sparq-policy

issues.body:
The test's comment states "Even though the policy evaluator permits the use request, its action has no single WAC mode, so no grant reaches the real query path" — but the only assertion is `assert!(!use_outcome.granted)`. `granted == false` is produced by two structurally different paths in `materialize_permission`: the deny/ambiguous early return at crates/sparq-solid/src/odrl_bridge.rs:356-358 (`BridgeOutcome::denied(decision.unmet_constraints)`), and the unmapped-action return at odrl_bridge.rs:362-366. The test cannot tell them apart.

Consequence: if the policy evaluator regressed such that an `odrl:use` request no longer matched an `odrl:use` permission, this test would stay green while the documented contract ("the request is permitted but the ACTION is unmapped") silently stopped being exercised — a false-green on the exact invariant the PR exists to pin. The subsequent `query_as(...).rows.len() == 0` assertion does not help, since it is also satisfied by a plain deny. The pre-existing test 6 at least asserts `!out.reasons.is_empty()`; the new test drops even that.
issues.fix_hint: Assert the discriminating reason string, which is stable and distinct: `assert!(use_outcome.reasons.iter().any(|r| r.contains("no WAC/ACP mode mapping")), "expected an unmapped-action refusal, not a plain deny: {use_outcome:?}");` (see the format! at crates/sparq-solid/src/odrl_bridge.rs:363-365). Optionally also assert `use_outcome.mode.is_none()` and `use_outcome.grant_triple.is_none()`. A quick mutation check confirms the value: flipping `action_to_mode`'s `use` arm to `Mode::Read` should turn this test red on the grant assertion, and stubbing the evaluator to deny should turn it red on the new reason assertion — currently only the first goes red.
issues.title: New test cannot distinguish "unmapped action" from "policy denied", so its central claim is untested

issues.body: The `odrl:use` half repeats `unmapped_action_materializes_nothing` (test 6, same policy shape, same request, same `!granted` conclusion), and the `odrl:read` half repeats `round_trip_through_enforcement` (test 3), down to the identical `sel` string and the `rows.len() == 1` assertion against `read_policy()`. The only genuinely new coverage is the single `query_as(&alice, Mode::Read, sel).rows.len() == 0` line for the unmapped `use` case — i.e. that an unmapped action yields nothing through the query path specifically, rather than only through `accessible`. That is worth having, but the surrounding duplication adds maintenance surface without adding signal.
issues.fix_hint: Optional. Either keep the test as the named, greppable home of the sq-lrtc3.2 contract (defensible — a documented contract deserves a test named after it), or trim it to the delta: drop the `read_store` half (already covered verbatim by test 3) and add the one `query_as == 0` assertion for the `use` case to test 6, leaving a short doc comment cross-referencing sq-lrtc3.2. Do not resolve this by deleting the `use`-side `query_as` assertion — that is the only new coverage in the test.
issues.title: Test 6a largely duplicates existing tests 3 and 6

verdict.summary:
Doc-and-test-only PR recording the sq-lrtc3.2 decision: a SPARQL query is expressed with the standard `odrl:read` action; sparq mints no profile-specific query action IRI, and an `odrl:use` request stays unmapped. The documented contract matches the implementation exactly — `action_to_mode` (crates/sparq-solid/src/odrl_bridge.rs:172-184) maps read/display/present/print/play to Mode::Read and returns None for `use`, and the bridge maps the REQUEST action at odrl_bridge.rs:361-366, so the 'hierarchy is the evaluator's concern, not the bridge's' framing is accurate and consistent with the pre-existing test 6. The new test is not vacuous: it exercises the real `materialize_odrl_permission` -> `query_as` enforcement path on a pod with no static ACL, and the read half is a genuine positive control (1 row) against the use half (0 rows); it would go red if the bridge ever started mapping `use` to Read. README/SKILL prose is preserved on reflow, net README line count is unchanged (readme-template cap unaffected), MD013 is disabled so the long lines are fine, and no ZK/MPC claim is introduced.

One blocking defect: SKILL.md's normative closing sentence instructs callers to write `Request::new(ODRL_READ)`, but no `ODRL_READ` constant is exported from sparq-solid or sparq-policy — the only definitions in the repo are private consts inside gui/src-tauri and sparq-lws-core. The SKILL's own example three paragraphs earlier correctly uses the literal IRI, so the new sentence both contradicts that example and sends readers to a symbol that does not compile. In a PR whose entire deliverable is a documented contract, the normative instruction naming a nonexistent API is a real defect. Also flagged: the new test asserts only `!granted` for the `use` case while its comment asserts the evaluator permits the request, so it cannot distinguish 'unmapped action' from 'policy denied' — the documented claim is under-pinned by one cheap assertion.
